ev.q: During 1980--2000, the black-white ratio of infant mortality increased 25.0% (from 2.0 to 2.5).
the LBW rate increased 2.4% for blacks (from 12.7% to 13.0%)
infant mortality declined 45.2% for all races during 1980--2000 (from 12.6 to 6.9 deaths per 1,000 live births)
the percentage of LBW infants increased 11.8% and that of VLBW infants increased 24.3%
infant mortality declined 45.2% for all races during 1980--2000
the decline was greater for whites than for blacks
increasing 22.4% (from 0.85 to 1.04) for MLBW infants and 22.3% (from 0.94 to 1.15) for VLBW infants
CDC analyzed race-specific infant mortality data for 1980--1999
This report describes trends in mortality and birth weight among black and white infants
To assess progress toward meeting these national objectives, CDC analyzed birth and death certificate data

methods_quotes.q: Trends in LBW and VLBW were calculated by using birth certificate data for 1980--2000
BWSMRs were calculated from linked birth and infant death files for 1983--1991 and 1995--1999
Both race-specific LBW/VLBW data and BWSMRs were calculated by using the race of the mother.
Mortality data based on race of infant as numerator and race of mother as denominator.
